key_insight: A new Japanese multi-turn stroke-care benchmark showed that only 2 of 18 evaluated LLMs met the preset safety threshold, highlighting major variability in real-world clinical conversation performance.
clinical_relevance: For stroke workflows, the findings suggest LLMs may support history-taking or triage only when rigorously tested for critical safety failures such as inappropriate tPA use or missing airway stabilization.
method: 10 Japanese stroke and related-condition cases were created for multi-turn physician-style dialogue.
A board-certified neurosurgeon served as simulated patient and evaluator; cases were scored across history-taking and action phases.
Eighteen LLMs were tested in October 2025 and June 2026 against a safety threshold of ≥80% overall with zero critical mistakes.
evidence_signal: Claude Fable 5 scored highest at 87.4% with zero critical mistakes, followed by Claude Opus 4.7 at 80.3%, while 11 models produced 17 critical mistakes.
watch_item: Because the benchmark uses only 10 specialist-designed cases, results may not generalize to broader real-world stroke presentations or deployment settings.
paper_title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
